chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs Tamattu' in the months of Hajj and then stays in Mecca until Hajj arrives, upon him is a sheep. And whoever performs Tamattu' in other than the months of Hajj and then stays (as a resident) until Hajj arrives, there is no dam (blood sacrifice) upon him; it is a single Hajj, and the Udhiyah (sacrifice) is upon the people of the cities (Ahl al-AmSar).'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If he lacks the sacrifice but has the means to buy it, he leaves it with a trustworthy person from the people of Mecca so that he may buy a sacrifice for him with it and slaughter it on his behalf in Dhu al-Hijjah. If he cannot do that, he sends it on his behalf in Dhu al-Hijjah of the coming year when the time for slaughter arrives.
Then he narrated that - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Regarding a Mutamatti' who finds the price but does not find the sheep, he said: 'He leaves the price with some of the people of Mecca and orders him to buy for him and slaughter on his behalf, and it suffices for him. If Dhu al-Hijjah passes, he delays that to the following Dhu al-Hijjah.'

key_terms.أَشْهُرُ اَلْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and the first ten days of Muharram)
key_terms.أَهْلُ اَلْأَمْصَارِ: People of the cities/provinces (residents of Mecca or nearby)
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Single Hajj (Hajj al-Qiran or Mufrad context)
key_terms.حَجُّ اَلتَّمَتُّعِ: Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of pilgrimage combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood sacrifice (often referring to a camel or cow)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the sacrifice for Hajj al-Tamattu' if the pilgrim cannot afford the animal at the time?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the distinction between the sacrificial obligation for Hajj al-Tamattu' performed within the Hajj months versus outside them, noting that the latter is treated as a single Hajj without an immediate blood offering. It further provides practical juristic guidance for pilgrims lacking immediate liquidity, permitting them to deposit funds with trustworthy locals in Mecca to secure the Hady, or defer the sacrifice to the following year if necessary. This reflects the Shia emphasis on flexibility in fulfilling ritual obligations based on financial capacity and timing.
